# Example resources

Real OpenPGP keys and files produced by the tests, kept so you can open them and try them with `gpg`.

> These keys are throwaway test fixtures protected by the passphrase `correct horse`. Never use them for anything real.

## Alice - generated by PGPKit

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `alice.public.asc` / `alice.public.gpg` | Public key, armored text / binary |
| `alice.private.asc` / `alice.private.gpg` | Private key (locked by the passphrase), armored text / binary |
| `message.txt` | The original plaintext |
| `message.txt.gpg` | `message.txt` encrypted to Alice, binary |
| `message.txt.asc` | The same encrypted message, armored text |
| `message.decrypted.txt` | The result of decrypting `message.txt.gpg` |
| `message.txt.sig` / `message.txt.sig.asc` | Detached signature of `message.txt`, binary / armored |

## Bob - generated by the `gpg` command line

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `bob.public.asc` / `bob.private.asc` | Key pair created with `gpg --quick-generate-key` |
| `gnupg-plain.txt` | Plaintext |
| `gnupg-encrypted.txt.gpg` | `gnupg-plain.txt` encrypted by `gpg`, then decrypted by PGPKit in the tests |
| `sdk-to-bob.txt.gpg` | A message encrypted by PGPKit for Bob |
| `sdk-to-bob.decrypted.txt` | That message decrypted by `gpg` |

## Try it with gpg

```sh
export GNUPGHOME="$(mktemp -d)" && chmod 700 "$GNUPGHOME"
gpg --batch --pinentry-mode loopback --passphrase "correct horse" --import alice.private.asc
gpg --batch --pinentry-mode loopback --passphrase "correct horse" --decrypt message.txt.gpg
gpg --verify message.txt.sig message.txt
```

## Regenerate

The files are committed, and the normal test run only reads them. To create new keys and files:

```sh
PGPKIT_GENERATE_EXAMPLES=1 xcrun swift test --filter ExampleResourcesGenerator
```
